summary:
Maluku stands under Indonesia's national framework. Both sources audited for this province are national in scope, and neither records a Maluku-specific ordinance, police operation, protection scheme or service, so the assessment rests on the national picture those sources document.

The penal code signed on 6 December 2022 took effect on 2 January 2026 and criminalises sexual activity between adults outside marriage. The Human Dignity Trust country profile records a maximum of two years' imprisonment, while the national overview gives up to one year where an immediate family member lodges a complaint; because same-sex marriage is not recognised, all sexual activity by same-sex couples falls within that outside-marriage restriction.

Legal gender recognition is available only after sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and only 'male' and 'female' sex descriptors are recognised, with no third-gender or X marker. Since June 2021 the Ministry of Home Affairs has run outreach issuing transgender Indonesians electronic ID cards in nine provinces as the document route.

National law provides no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections, and the Constitution is silent on sexual orientation and gender identity. On 14 December 2017 the Constitutional Court rejected 5-4 a petition to criminalise homosexuality; the Sharia-based criminalisation outlier is Aceh, not Maluku.

Reporting in August 2026 describes growing repression of Indonesia's transgender community, with vigilante mobs attacking trans people as the government takes steps to codify anti-LGBT provisions. The page records that Indonesia voted against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity, and that a 2023 Pew Research survey found 95% of Indonesians oppose same-sex marriage.
tangentialFactors:
The national picture includes police raids on LGBT gatherings, including a June 2025 villa raid near Bogor that arrested 75 people, and a presidential decree of October 2025 listing LGBTQ+ people as a non-military national threat. These events occurred outside Maluku but indicate the enforcement climate a visitor to Maluku would enter.

Indonesia's 2006 Law Against Pornography and Pornoaction punishes material showing or suggesting same-sex relations with up to seven years' imprisonment, and the national broadcasting commission banned normalising LGBTQ content in March 2016. Website and app blocks covering LGBTQ-related terms, including Grindr, are national.
localsOnly:
Transgender residents of Maluku seeking legal gender recognition must undergo sex-reassignment surgery and obtain judicial approval, and must carry either a 'male' or 'female' sex descriptor on official documents. The Ministry of Home Affairs electronic ID card outreach since June 2021 has been implemented in nine provinces; whether Maluku is among them is not stated in the sources.

Residents have no statutory protection against discrimination or harassment on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, and the Constitution does not address either. Complaints under the outside-marriage provision of the penal code can be initiated by an immediate family member.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Maluku has its own provincial ordinance, police operation, protection scheme or support service is unresolved: the sources audited are national in scope and record no Maluku-specific finding. Whether Maluku is one of the nine provinces covered by the Ministry of Home Affairs electronic ID card outreach is also not sourced.

The sources give two different maximum penalties under the outside-marriage provision (two years in one, one year on family complaint in the other); both figures are reported as they appear and the discrepancy is unresolved.
